assigned_method_paragraph: Unmapped permeable faults hosting concealed hydrothermal upflow across the Great Basin (EPSG:32611) occupy two physically distinct crustal cover regimes that single-regime detectors trade off against one another (DSLUP-3D reached HIDE-RECOVER-v3.0 = 0.125925 and SGMC-CAL-v3.0 = 0.098140 on shallow bedrock/range-front corridors but fell to 0.073458 on concealed Z_b >= 250 m piedmont faults C-PIED-v1.0, whereas DARP-MT10 reached C-PIED-v1.0 = 0.140750 +39.1% over the 0.2778 champion yet starved shallow contacts to SGMC-CAL = 0.043178 due to cubic piedmont_habitat_prior over-damping IR-DARP-CREST-OVERDAMP-08). We partition out-of-quadrant (1.5 km-collared, cross-segment-purged) fault-conduit inference continuously by sedimentary cover thickness w_basin(Z_b) = clip((Z_b - 120 m)/380 m, 0, 1) into a Shallow Range-Front & Void-Bridged 1m/3m/10m Geomorphic Specialist (1 - w_basin) and a Concealed Basin-Margin & Blind Geothermal Fault-Valve Specialist (w_basin) incorporating cohort-detrended 1m-to-2m vertical probe conductive temperature gradients, cold-aquifer (<28 C) silica/cation geothermometer disequilibrium, Quaternary silica-cemented sand / explosion fault-valve loci, 2-D Fourier Poisson gravity-minus-pseudogravity hydrothermal decoupling ridges, and off-catalogue accommodation-zone strike-divergence hinges, allocated via 300 m triangular-kernel CELF submodular greedy placement (37,654 dots).
